title: Police are pulling people over because license plate cameras say their travel patterns look "suspicious"
summary: TechSpot summarizes an ACLU report describing traffic stops based solely on 'suspicious' travel patterns derived from Flock and other ALPR databases, citing incidents from 2025 including a road-tripper stopped by an FBI agent and a Wisconsin-Michigan driver suspected of marijuana trafficking. It notes an Oklahoma judge calling such a stop unconstitutional mass surveillance, and mentions a Florida bill to require warrants for ALPR database searches.

key_quotes.quote: The ACLU recently outlined a pattern of police traffic stops based solely on data from Flock cameras and other license plate readers.
an Oklahoma judge called a similar stop unconstitutional indiscriminate mass surveillance, even though it led to the seizure of 91 pounds of meth.
a Florida representative recently introduced a bill to require warrants to search ALPR databases.
